title: The Exam-Week Cold
briefing: Noah, 16, sleeps about five hours a night during finals week and feels stressed from Monday to Friday. On Friday he catches the cold that's been going around his class. When the same kind of cold went around in October, he didn't catch it at all.
question: Why did the cold get through this week, when it didn't in October?

clues.title: Five hours a night
clues.text: He studied until 1 a.m. every night and his alarm went off at 6. Normally he sleeps about eight hours.
clues.shows: far less sleep than usual, night after night

visual.unit: hours of sleep, normal week → finals week

clues.title: Stressed all week
clues.text: His heart raced before every exam and he couldn't switch off at night, worrying about grades. It lasted all five days.
clues.shows: stress hormones staying high for days

clues.title: Caught it on Friday
clues.text: Half his class had the sniffles that week, and on Friday he caught it too. In October the same kind of cold went around and he stayed well.
clues.shows: his defences being weaker this week than usual

clues.title: Two friends, two results
clues.text: Maya was just as stressed but slept eight hours a night — she only got a slight sniffle. Kai stayed up late on a relaxed art project — he caught a mild cold, lighter than Noah's.
clues.shows: less sleep and more stress each weakening defence, and worst together

hypotheses.text: Not enough sleep weakened his immune system.
hypotheses.flaw: Sleep matters, but Maya slept eight hours and still got a sniffle under stress — and Kai, short on sleep but relaxed, got off lighter than Noah.

hypotheses.text: Both: night after night of short sleep and a week of stress hormones each weakened his immune defences, so together they let the cold going around get through.

hypotheses.flaw: Stress matters, but Kai wasn't stressed and still caught a cold after his late nights.

hypotheses.text: Studying too hard gives you colds.
hypotheses.flaw: Colds come from viruses passed between people — the same kind was around in October. What changed this week was his defence, not the studying itself.

prediction.prompt: During a stressful week, as Noah gets more hours of sleep each night — from 4 up to 9 — what happens to his immune defence?

second.question: If the stress of finals vanished but his sleep stayed the same, would his immune defence go up or down?

transfer.context: During tech week for the school play, the cast rehearses until 11 p.m. every night and everyone is nervous about opening night. By Friday half the cast has the cold going around backstage.
options: Short sleep and stress together weakened their immune defences, so the cold going around got past them.
transfer.retryHint: Noah's two friends each had only one of his two problems — what happened to each of them?
transfer.explanation: The cast has both of Noah's problems at once: late nights cut their sleep, and opening-night nerves keep stress hormones high. Each lowers immune defence; together they let the cold going around backstage get through.

takeaway: Your immune system needs sleep, and long-lasting stress pushes it down. Each alone weakens your defences a little; together they open the door for whatever cold is going around.
